newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weaker on month-end dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weaker on month-end dollar demand.

text.p: The Mexican closed weaker across the board on Friday due to traditional month-end demand for dollars, traders said.
"We are at the end of the month and many dealers are closing their books, and that fuels demand for dollars," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.7 and 2.3 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.180/7.9220 and 7.9140/7.9190 per dollar.
Dealers said the peso had recovered some ground lost to the dollar in earlier trade on falling U.S. long bond yields.
"Long bond yields fell, and that eased market pressure,' another trader said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury Bond had gained 25/32 in late trade to yield 6.91 percent.

Dealers also noted that month-end demand was light but sufficient to sway a market where volume thinned due to the absence of many brokers who had travelled to a foreign exchange dealers' convention at the Caribbean beach resort of Cancun.
"Every one squared their books and left; volume was very light," one dealer said.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.85 of a centavo weaker at 7.8920/7.8950 per dollar, after lagging behind the market.
